quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to exit the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive slowly and carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrians crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low overpass ahead. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, and ease back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, and ease back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Release the gas pedal and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road with a small turn of the steering wheel. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck body.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are very large. The driver cannot see your car behind them. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for work zone violations are the same as fines for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for the work zone.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the work zone.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones. Be ready to slow down or stop for equipment. Careful driving through work zones keeps everyone safe—drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as you can.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that pedestrians may be crossing. Stop and remain stopped for pedestrians in a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When passing a car, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to return.
When you see the passed car behind you by looking over your shoulder.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is safe distance between your vehicle and the passed vehicle before returning to your lane. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive.
Drive slower and leave more space between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and leave more space between cars.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snowy or icy roads. Increase the distance between your vehicle and other cars. These are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. On interstates, you cannot back up or make U-turns, so you must continue to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow means the protected turn is about to end. You must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mark areas where passing is not allowed. Two solid yellow lines mean no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the wheels and causes you to lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the wheels and causes you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice locks the wheels, so you lose control of steering. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Entering traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal for any movement to the left or right. Signal when changing lanes, parking, entering traffic, or passing.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to prevent hydroplaning. Driving fast causes tires to ride on water and lose grip with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where people, animals, or other vehicles may cross.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Expect the unexpected.
Construction workers will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extreme caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed in both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed on hills.
Passing is allowed during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the force of impact in a collision.

questions.question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Apply your brakes hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: Traffic next to the broken line may cross to pass. Traffic next to the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: With a probationary license or instructional permit, when can you use your cell phone while driving?

options.text: When answering a call.
As long as you don't text.
When reporting an emergency.
Anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: When reporting an emergency.
questions.explanation: With a probationary license or instructional permit, using a cell phone while driving is illegal in Wisconsin. The only exception is to report an emergency.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: You should drive at the maximum posted speed limit only:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
When conditions are ideal.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under perfect conditions. Drive at the speed of surrounding traffic, up to the limit. Safe driving speed is the responsibility of all drivers.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.
Pass at a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, where solid yellow lines are on your side, when the car ahead stopped for a pedestrian, or in work zones.

questions.question: A broken yellow line in the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, a broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can see clearly again. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of other cars on the road.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first starts to rain. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or quick stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and also:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in the lane you want to enter. This helps you avoid other drivers who may also be moving into that lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at about the same speed.
When one lane of traffic moves faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster increases collision risk. Driving slower also increases risk because it can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign means you are approaching railroad tracks. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left side mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Make sure your blind spot is clear. Never rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder.
Look over your right shoulder when changing right. Look over your left shoulder when changing left.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder when changing right. Look over your left shoulder when changing left.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with lights flashing and stop arm extended, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle has room to cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle has room to cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough room to get all the way across before driving onto the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no oncoming traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a steady red light only if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is turning left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is turning left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right when there is an available passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You may also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, release the accelerator first to let your vehicle slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly to stop.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what is true?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt than on asphalt or concrete. Slow down on these roads. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than cars.
They do not need more space to turn than cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.
